RESUMO

Introdução
:

A

osteogênese

imperfeita

(OI)

é

uma

doença

genética

rara,

caracterizada

por

alterações

no

colágeno

tipo

I,

que

resultam

em

fragilidade

óssea

e

manifestações

sistêmicas,

incluindo

perda

auditiva.

Esta

pode

apresentar-se

nas

formas

condutiva,

neurossensorial

ou

mista,

geralmente

de

forma

progressiva

e

bilateral.

A

timpanometria

com

sonda

de

226

Hz

é

um

método

objetivo

para

avaliação

da

orelha

média,

porém

há

poucos

estudos

sobre

a

evolução

longitudinal

de

seus

parâmetros

em

indivíduos

com

OI.

Objetivo
:

Descrever

e

analisar

os

resultados

da

timpanometria

com

sonda

de

226

Hz

em

indivíduos

com

OI.

Métodos
:

Estudo

prospectivo,

longitudinal

e

observacional,

realizado

em

um

centro

de

referência

do

sul

do

Brasil.

Foram

incluídos

indivíduos

com

diagnóstico

confirmado

de

OI

e

idade

mínima

de

cinco

anos.

Os

participantes

foram

submetidos

à

meatoscopia,

timpanometria

com

sonda

de

226

Hz

e

audiometria

tonal

limiar.

Foram

analisados

os

parâmetros

timpanométricos

de

complacência,

pressão

do

pico

timpanométrico

(PPT)

e

tipo

de

curva.

Dados

audiológicos

prévios

também

foram

incorporados

à

análise

longitudinal.

O

estudo

compreendeu

duas

etapas:

uma

análise

transversal

e

outra

longitudinal.

Na

análise

transversal,

os

dados

foram

processados

no

SPSS®

versão

27,

com

nível

de

significância

de

5%.

Utilizaram-se

os

testes

de

Wilcoxon,

McNemar,

Kruskal-Wallis,

Dunn

e

qui-quadrado,

conforme

a

natureza

das

variáveis.

Na

análise

longitudinal,

foram

empregados

métodos

estatísticos

para

medidas

repetidas,

considerando

a

evolução

dos

parâmetros

ao

longo

do

acompanhamento.

Resultados:

Após

a

aplicação

dos

critérios

de

inclusão

e

exclusão,

a

amostra

foi

composta

por

245

orelhas

no

primeiro

estudo

.

Houve

predominância

do

sexo

feminino

e

do

tipo

I

de

osteogênese

imperfeita,

com

idade

variando

entre

9

e

33

anos.

A

complacência

variou

de

0,45

ml

a

0,95

ml

e

a

PPT

entre

–26

daPa

e

–2

daPa,

sendo

a

curva

tipo

A

a

mais

frequente.

Observou-se

aumento

da

complacência

com

a

idade

e

valores

mais

elevados

no

grupo

com

OI

leve.

A

pressão

foi

mais

negativa

nos

participantes

com

alteração

condutiva,

e

a

distribuição

dos

tipos

de

curva

diferiu

conforme

o

perfil

audiológico.

No

estudo

longitudinal

foram

avaliadas

151

orelhas.

Observou-se

redução

significativa

da

complacência

no

terceiro

momento

de

avaliação

(p=0,012),

sem

variação

significativa

da

PPT

ao

longo

do

tempo.

Houve

aumento

progressivo

de

curvas

timpanométricas

alteradas,

embora

a

curva

tipo

A

tenha

permanecido

predominante.

A

complacência

apresentou

associação

significativa

com

faixa

etária

e

tipo

de

perda

auditiva,

sendo

mais

elevada

nos

indivíduos

com

alteração

condutiva.

A

PPT

variou

conforme

a

gravidade

da

OI,

com

valores

menos

negativos

nos

casos

leves.

Conclusões
:

Embora

a

curva

timpanométrica

tipo

A

permaneça

predominante,

os

parâmetros

numéricos

da

timpanometria

evidenciam

variações

relacionadas

à

idade,

à

gravidade

da

OI

e

ao

perfil

audiológico.

Esses

resultados

reforçam

a

importância

do

monitoramento

audiológico

longitudinal

em

indivíduos

com

osteogênese

imperfeita.

ABSTRACT

Introduction:

Osteogenesis

imperfecta

(OI)

is

a

rare

genetic

disorder

characterized

by

alterations

in

type

I

collagen,

resulting

in

bone

fragility

and

systemic

manifestations,

including

hearing

loss.

Hearing

loss

may

occur

in

conductive,

sensorineural,

or

mixed

forms,

generally

progressing

bilaterally

over

time.

Tympanometry

using

a

226

Hz

probe

tone

is

an

objective

method

for

assessing

middle

ear

function;

however,

few

studies

have

investigated

the

longitudinal

evolution

of

its

parameters

in

individuals

with

OI.

Objective:

To

describe

and

analyze

the

results

of

226

Hz

probe

tone

tympanometry

in

individuals

with

OI.

Methods:

This

prospective,

longitudinal,

observational

study

was

conducted

at

a

referral

center

in

southern

Brazil.

Individuals

with

a

confirmed

diagnosis

of

OI

and

aged

five

years

or

older

were

included.

Participants

underwent

otoscopy,

226

Hz

probe

tone

tympanometry,

and

pure-tone

audiometry.

Tympanometric

parameters

analyzed

included

compliance,

tympanometric

peak

pressure

(TPP),

and

tympanogram

type.

Previous

audiological

data

were

also

incorporated

into

the

longitudinal

analysis.

The

study

comprised

two

stages:

a

cross-sectional

analysis

and

a

longitudinal

analysis.

In

the

cross-sectional

analysis,

data

were

processed

using

SPSS®

version

27,

adopting

a

significance

level

of

5%.

Wilcoxon,

McNemar,

Kruskal–Wallis,

Dunn,

and

chi-square

tests

were

applied

according

to

the

nature

of

the

variables.

In

the

longitudinal

analysis,

statistical

methods

for

repeated

measures

were

used

to

evaluate

changes

in

tympanometric

parameters

over

time.

Results:

After

applying

the

inclusion

and

exclusion

criteria,

the

sample

comprised

245

ears

in

the

first

article

and

151

in

the

second.

Although

osteogenesis

imperfecta

is

a

rare

condition,

the

substantial

number

of

ears

evaluated

is

justified

by

the

fact

that

the

study

was

conducted

at

the

reference

outpatient

clinic

of

Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre,

in

southern

Brazil.

There

was

a

predominance

of

females

and

type

I

osteogenesis

imperfecta,

with

ages

ranging

from

9

to

33

years.

Type

A

tympanometric

curve

was

the

most

frequent

finding

at

all

evaluated

time

points.

Compliance

values

ranged

from

0.45

mL

to

0.95

mL,

showing

an

increase

with

age

and

higher

values

in

individuals

with

mild

disease

and

those

with

conductive

hearing

loss;

a

significant

reduction

was

observed

at

the

third

evaluation

time

point.

Tympanometric

peak

pressure

did

not

show

significant

variation

over

time;

however,

it

was

more

negative

in

participants

with

conductive

hearing

loss

and

less

negative

in

mild

cases.

Conclusions:

Although

type

A

tympanometric

curves

remained

predominant,

numerical

tympanometric

parameters

varied

according

to

age,

disease

severity,

and

audiological

profile.

These

findings

highlight

the

importance

of

longitudinal

audiological

monitoring

in

individuals

with

osteogenesis

imperfecta.

ABSTRACT

Introduction:

Osteogenesis

imperfecta

(OI)

is

a

rare

genetic

disorder

characterized

by

alterations

in

type

I

collagen,

resulting

in

bone

fragility

and

systemic

manifestations,

including

hearing

loss.

Hearing

loss

may

occur

in

conductive,

sensorineural,

or

mixed

forms,

generally

progressing

bilaterally

over

time.

Tympanometry

using

a

226

Hz

probe

tone

is

an

objective

method

for

assessing

middle

ear

function;

however,

few

studies

have

investigated

the

longitudinal

evolution

of

its

parameters

in

individuals

with

OI.

Objective:

To

describe

and

analyze

the

results

of

226

Hz

probe

tone

tympanometry

in

individuals

with

OI.

Methods:

This

prospective,

longitudinal,

observational

study

was

conducted

at

a

referral

center

in

southern

Brazil.

Individuals

with

a

confirmed

diagnosis

of

OI

and

aged

five

years

or

older

were

included.

Participants

underwent

otoscopy,

226

Hz

probe

tone

tympanometry,

and

pure-tone

audiometry.

Tympanometric

parameters

analyzed

included

compliance,

tympanometric

peak

pressure

(TPP),

and

tympanogram

type.

Previous

audiological

data

were

also

incorporated

into

the

longitudinal

analysis.

The

study

comprised

two

stages:

a

cross-sectional

analysis

and

a

longitudinal

analysis.

In

the

cross-sectional

analysis,

data

were

processed

using

SPSS®

version

27,

adopting

a

significance

level

of

5%.

Wilcoxon,

McNemar,

Kruskal–Wallis,

Dunn,

and

chi-square

tests

were

applied

according

to

the

nature

of

the

variables.

In

the

longitudinal

analysis,

statistical

methods

for

repeated

measures

were

used

to

evaluate

changes

in

tympanometric

parameters

over

time.

Results:

After

applying

the

inclusion

and

exclusion

criteria,

the

sample

comprised

245

ears

in

the

first

article

and

151

in

the

second.

Although

osteogenesis

imperfecta

is

a

rare

condition,

the

substantial

number

of

ears

evaluated

is

justified

by

the

fact

that

the

study

was

conducted

at

the

reference

outpatient

clinic

of

Hospital

de

Clínicas

de

Porto

Alegre,

in

southern

Brazil.

There

was

a

predominance

of

females

and

type

I

osteogenesis

imperfecta,

with

ages

ranging

from

9

to

33

years.

Type

A

tympanometric

curve

was

the

most

frequent

finding

at

all

evaluated

time

points.

Compliance

values

ranged

from

0.45

mL

to

0.95

mL,

showing

an

increase

with

age

and

higher

values

in

individuals

with

mild

disease

and

those

with

conductive

hearing

loss;

a

significant

reduction

was

observed

at

the

third

evaluation

time

point.

Tympanometric

peak

pressure

did

not

show

significant

variation

over

time;

however,

it

was

more

negative

in

participants

with

conductive

hearing

loss

and

less

negative

in

mild

cases.

Conclusions:

Although

type

A

tympanometric

curves

remained

predominant,

numerical

tympanometric

parameters

varied

according

to

age,

disease

severity,

and

audiological

profile.

These

findings

highlight

the

importance

of

longitudinal

audiological

monitoring

in

individuals

with

osteogenesis

imperfecta.
